newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-At standoff as all eyes on India.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-At standoff as all eyes on India.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil and jet fuel buyers were at a stand off on Thursday, waiting for direction from India's gas oil import tender for September, and deterred by high market offers, traders said.
"I don't think there a lot of outlets and buyers will want cheaper numbers," one trader said.
"There is a little stand off coming into the end of the week with the IOC (Indian Oil Corp) gas oil tender about to be awarded and people are looking for direction from it."
Traders said the market was also concerned with direction amid the firming western gas oil market.
The IOC tender closed on Thursday and was expected to be awarded late on Friday.

But after taking only 165,000 tonnes for August deliveries, traders were not optimistic for a big award for September, which is not a traditionally high demand month amid the monsoon. They estimated the award would be around 250,000-300,000 tonnes.
Some traders noted that a lower award has been factored in by the market and if IOC were to take more it would help to drive gas oil prices higher.
Traders said since market conditions have not changed drastically since the awards of August cargoes, they expected offers to be around the same level as in the last tender.

The swaps market rose on the back of firmer crudes and higher western prices with sellers emerging in large numbers when values for August hit $23.00 per barrel. Trades for August were seen earlier at $23.15 and $23.10, before coming down to $23.00 and $22.95.

But traders said physical buyers stayed away amid higher offers. Three gas oil offers were seen around $22.95 and another three offers at the same level for jet fuel for mid-August liftings free-on-board.

The jet fuel market was also seeking direction from Taiwan's purchase tender for September delivery. Offers were aggressive at around $191-$192 per tonne, c-and-f basis, compared with around $197 awarded for the August-delivery cargo.

But Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) might not award the tender as its refining and marketing units were seeking a second-half September cargo because of high stocks, while the offers were for first-half September, CPC source said.
The jet fuel market also saw offers from Kuwait which was seeking at 20-30 discounts to Singapore spot quotes, fob basis, while buyers were seeking deeper discounts.
